The interplay between these operators creates a dynamic system of conditional information states. Privilege segregation acts as a topological barrier, custodial preservation as an integrity constraint, and disclosure control as a probabilistic filter. Failure modes include: (1) privilege violation when P=1 but C=0, (2) preservation failure when R=0, and (3) inadvertent disclosure when D>0.5. These operators exhibit duality in their enforcement mechanisms—privilege and preservation are both reactive to external inputs, while disclosure control is proactive. The system's stability depends on maintaining consistent boundary conditions across all three operators.
